help_route: Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff for help to find an age-appropriate route. No named service, number, website or online task is given. Seek help if a concern persists, worsens, affects everyday life or feels unsafe; you do not need a diagnosis first. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school's urgent procedure.
step_out: Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
marking: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Explicit short definitions, worked example, glossary, visible model, task frames and one chosen step. Flexible grouping for a pair; reduced written load and extra processing time.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Choice, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing, exact scribe and readback. Pair discussion optional; no requirement for speech or eye contact.
adaptations.SEMH: Predict the sequence, keep all stories invented and mild, offer a quiet supervised pause and supported return. No public feeling check. Story body map and private plan can be blank, fictional or passed; never collect personal details.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Keep the room calm and the usual access and health plans. No induced pressure or noise. Offer one small familiar movement, adapted to access and comfortable range; observing or passing is equal. Breathing stays gentle at own pace, with no holds. Stop discomfort and seek staff help.
adaptations.EAL: Pre-teach stress, sign and reframing with short plain meanings and the invented story. Allow planning in any language, pointing, glossary and usual language support. No personal explanation is required.

where_this_leads: Next learning applies calm decision-making and help-seeking to safe choices online. Offer fictional learning to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping and evidence sufficiency.
title: Managing stress and change
subject: RSE
source_note: Date, period and exact outcome are from the owner brief, LAUNCH Weekly Spring row 149. The workbook was not reopened. Accepted Week 1 supplies format only. Current official public-health pages on stress, gentle breathing, reframing and young people's movement were checked for narrow factual teaching. Strategies are optional educational practice, not treatment or a clinical assessment. The campaign wording is preserved only as part of the exact outcome.

definitions.stress: A response to pressure or change. It can affect the body, thoughts, feelings and actions. A little pressure can help with a task; too much or lasting pressure can make daily life harder.
definitions.sign: A possible clue that someone may feel under pressure. Signs vary and can have other causes. A body map cannot diagnose stress or a condition.
definitions.reframing: Checking a thought against what is known and trying a fairer, more useful way to view the situation. It can include naming a real problem and asking for help.

key_points: Stress is a response to pressure or change, not a weakness.
Possible signs differ. They can have other causes. A map is not a diagnosis.
No one has to become stressed to practise a strategy.
A strategy may help some people; it is not a guaranteed fix. Support and changes to the situation can still be needed.

scene.title: A changed task order
scene.text: An invented learner hears that two familiar tasks will happen in a different order. Their shoulders feel tense, their stomach feels fluttery and it is hard to focus. They think, “I will get every part wrong.” The tasks are familiar and school staff can explain the first step. Nothing unsafe has happened.
scene.model: The learner might be responding to the changed plan. Tense shoulders, a fluttery stomach and poor focus are possible signs; they can have other causes. A fairer thought is, “The order changed. I know parts of these tasks. I can ask for the first step.” The learner can try a gentle strategy and ask staff to make the plan clear.
discussion: Which possible signs are in the invented story?
What is known, and what does the learner predict?
Which strategy or practical support could fit?

body_map.title: Stress signs in an invented story
body_map.instruction: Use only the invented learner. Draw lines from the three story clues to the map. Write or place the words. A list or pointing route is equal. Do not map your own symptoms.
body_map.note: These are possible clues, not proof of stress or a diagnosis. People can show different signs or none that others can see. The map is a learning diagram, not a test.

strategies.name: Gentle breathing
strategies.steps: Sit or stand in your usual supported position. Let an easy breath come in and out at your own pace. Keep breathing comfortable. No hold, forced deep breath, set rate or count. Try briefly, then return to usual breathing.
strategies.adapt: Eyes can stay open. Stop and tell staff if uncomfortable or dizzy. You may observe, use normal breathing or pass.
strategies.model: The invented learner pauses and lets a few easy breaths come and go.

strategies.name: Reframing
strategies.steps: Use the invented thought: “I will get every part wrong.” What is known? The order changed, but the tasks are familiar. Try: “I know some parts. I can ask for the first step.” Say, point to, type or write the fairer thought.
strategies.adapt: A fairer thought need not be cheerful. It must fit the facts. Do not reframe harm as acceptable or dismiss a real problem. Asking for a clearer plan is valid.
strategies.model: “The order changed. I know some parts. I can ask for the first step.”

strategies.name: Accessible movement
strategies.steps: With staff agreement, try one small, familiar move that suits your access plan: a gentle hand move, a seated stretch or a few steps in the agreed clear space. Stay in a comfortable range.
strategies.adapt: No touch, exertion, balance challenge or performance target. Use a familiar alternative or observe/pass. Stop if painful or uncomfortable; follow usual health and access plans.
strategies.model: The invented learner uses an agreed short hand movement, then asks staff to explain the plan.

action_plan.instruction: Choose one possible strategy for a mild change, privately, or plan for the invented learner. Include practical support. No personal worry, symptom, health or family detail is needed. Keep the card. Blank or pass is valid.
fields: A mild change or cue, with no private detail
How to keep it safe and suited to me
Support by role that could help
If it does not help or I need more support
action_plan.model: For the invented learner: when a familiar task order changes, check a fairer thought and ask school staff for the first step. If that is not useful, ask for another explanation or the agreed supervised pause.
action_plan.rule: One useful choice and a support route. No promise to feel calm and no requirement to cope alone. Strategies do not replace help with the cause of pressure.

self_assessment.title: Learning self check
items: I can explain stress and a possible sign without diagnosing.
I can describe the three strategies and a safe choice or adaptation.
I can show a fairer thought and a route to support.
self_assessment.note: All boxes start blank. This checks learning, not feelings, symptoms or whether a strategy worked. Observing, adapting or passing is recorded fairly, without a health judgement.

safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of the lesson pack, book tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school's separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. Private plans are not collected, photographed, displayed or compared for assessment. Scribing the personal plan is only by agreement; the learner keeps it.
practice_rule: All class questions and optional pair talk use the invented learner. Offer each of the three brief strategy trials in the calm lesson; never create pressure, noise or an upsetting surprise. No pupil reports a personal symptom, worry or feeling. Adapt, observe or pass without explanation. Private plan stays with the pupil; staff assess fictional understanding only.
evidence: Record explanation of stress, three fictional body-map links, a fairer thought, safe strategy knowledge and a generic support route. Record each breathing/reframing/movement opportunity as tried, adapted, observed, passed or not observed; no pass is failure. Do not record symptoms, feelings, private plan content or claimed improvement. Distinguish usual access from actual adult content prompts. Use a work code, one NS and actual pupil response. E requires saved actual work; R requires Voice and Audience plus NS and own response.

routes.Supported: Use short word choices, story clues, pointing or exact scribe/readback. Match three story signs to map/list. Use a fairer-thought choice and one safe strategy choice. All three trials offered; access/adapt/observe/pass remain.
routes.Independent: Use the story to link three signs, explain a fairer thought and choose a safe strategy with a reason and support. All three trials offered. Usual aids stay.
routes.Aspire: Explain why clues are not a diagnosis. Compare two safe approaches to the invented change, test a practical barrier and keep one final choice with support. All three trials offered; extra reasoning never means more personal disclosure.

scaffolds.start: In the story, one clue is…

scaffolds.model: It may be stress, but it is not proof.
I link tense shoulders to the shoulder area.
Use a gentle move within the usual access plan.
Ask staff to show the first step.
A fairer thought fits what is known.

hinge.question: What can the story clues tell us?
hinge.A: They prove the learner has a condition.
hinge.B: They may show pressure, but can have other causes.
hinge.decision: Correct B. If A is chosen, explain that signs alone cannot establish a condition; re-model then use the parallel privately. No public answer round.

parallel.question: Which response fits the invented change?
parallel.A: Check the facts and ask staff to explain the first step.
parallel.B: Tell the learner to ignore every concern.
parallel.decision: Correct A. A fairer view can include real support. If unclear, keep the model and revisit later; do not label the learner.

misconceptions: Clues vary and can have other causes; no classroom diagnosis.
A strategy must work for everyone.
Access, context and preferences vary. Adapt or ask for support.
Reframing means pretending all is fine.
A fairer thought fits facts and can include a real problem and help.
timing: Calm set-up and discreet supervised pause route.

Teach stress with the invented change; one story check.
Private main and parallel check; reset15–16.
One NS and actual pupil response.
Fictional help route and supported close.

paragraphs: Stress learning guide
Managing stress & change (Children's MH Week).
Use the invented learner. You may say, point, draw, type or use your usual aid. A scribe can write your exact chosen words and read them back. Personal details are not needed.
Invented change

An invented learner hears that two familiar tasks will happen in a different order. Their shoulders feel tense, their stomach feels fluttery and it is hard to focus. They think, “I will get every part wrong.” The tasks are familiar and school staff can explain the first step. Nothing unsafe has happened.
In your book

Link the three story clues to the map or a list. Explain why clues are not proof. Try a fairer story thought, then choose a safe strategy and a support role. Keep the short story work you make during practice; no long new task is needed.
Model

The learner might be responding to the changed plan. Tense shoulders, a fluttery stomach and poor focus are possible signs; they can have other causes. A fairer thought is, “The order changed. I know parts of these tasks. I can ask for the first step.” The learner can try a gentle strategy and ask staff to make the plan clear.
Trial choices

Breathing, reframing and movement are all offered in the calm lesson. You can try an adapted option, observe or pass. No one has to feel stressed. A strategy need not make someone feel better to show learning.
Review
Use one next step on fictional work and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. The self-check is about learning. Keep your personal plan with you; it is not collected.
Staff learning record

Use a work code, not a name. Record fictional learning only. No private plan, symptoms, feelings, health/family history or disclosure details. Actual concerns go in the separate school safeguarding record.

No participation choice is failure. Do not infer symptoms, diagnosis, health or strategy effectiveness. Record not observed honestly. E requires saved actual work; R requires Voice and Audience, one NS and own response. Any disclosure goes to safeguarding lead through school procedure. Maintain the agreed supervised pause route.

paragraphs: Teacher and cover planner
Managing stress and change
Thursday 14 January 2027 · P4 · 40 minutes · Year A
LAUNCH · pair aged 14–16 · Spring 1 Week 2 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Exact outcome
Managing stress & change (Children's MH Week).
Source
Owner brief, LAUNCH Weekly Spring row 149. Accepted Week 1 supplies structure only. Workbook not reopened. Exact campaign wording is retained in the outcome only.
Purpose and success

Explain stress and possible signs without a diagnosis. Link story clues to a body map or list. Explore gentle breathing, reframing and accessible movement, with safe adaptations, then choose one useful option and support route. Personal plan is private; learning evidence is fictional.
Non specialist cover preparation

Read Staff Answers. Print one tier per learner, Support Cards pages 1–3, glossary and staff Evidence Sheet. Use books/usual aids. Quietly pre-agree the supervised pause route. Use calm fictional examples. Do not create pressure or ask personal symptom questions. Follow usual health, physical access and communication plans. No equipment, internet or special activity is needed.
Forty minute sequence
Resets at 15–16, 27–28 and 33–34 are inside the forty minutes. Pair talk is optional and fictional. Adapt, observe or pass is valid for each trial.
Teaching and response routes
Arrival and starter

0–4: calm set-up, preview and discreet pause route. 4–6: show the invented claim that stress affects only thoughts. Explain that body, feelings and actions can also be involved; no personal examples needed.
Model and checks

6–11: teach meanings using the invented changed-task-order story. Link possible clues without diagnosing. Check what is known versus predicted. 11–15: main hinge B, with parallel A if needed; record a private response. 15–16: reset. Usual aids and the visible model stay.
Map and three trials

16–19: link the three invented clues to the body map or list. 19–21: offer gentle own-pace breathing. 21–24: each learner checks the fictional thought and tries a fairer version in usual mode. 24–27: offer one small familiar movement suited to access and health plans. Show the safe options before each trial. Record tried/adapted/observed/passed/not observed, never a score or effect. 27–28: reset.
Private plan and evidence

28–30: invite a private plan card or fictional/blank/pass route. Keep it with the learner. 30–33: use the short fictional answer already made during practice and learning self-check; do not add a full new written task. 33–34: reset. 34–38: one NS and own reply. 38–40: generic support route and supported close.
Supported

Use short word choices, story clues, pointing or exact scribe/readback. Match three story signs to map/list. Use a fairer-thought choice and one safe strategy choice. All three trials offered; access/adapt/observe/pass remain.
Independent
Use the story to link three signs, explain a fairer thought and choose a safe strategy with a reason and support. All three trials offered. Usual aids stay.
Aspire

Explain why clues are not a diagnosis. Compare two safe approaches to the invented change, test a practical barrier and keep one final choice with support. All three trials offered; extra reasoning never means more personal disclosure.
Worked model and fade

The learner might be responding to the changed plan. Tense shoulders, a fluttery stomach and poor focus are possible signs; they can have other causes. A fairer thought is, “The order changed. I know parts of these tasks. I can ask for the first step.” The learner can try a gentle strategy and ask staff to make the plan clear. For the invented learner: when a familiar task order changes, check a fairer thought and ask school staff for the first step. If that is not useful, ask for another explanation or the agreed supervised pause. Show a model, then leave the choice/reason to the learner. Keep glossary, short frames and usual aids.
TA focus

I do: model non-diagnostic clues and safe trials. We do: offer a story word or frame. Independent: observe the fictional response and actual content prompts, retain usual aids, acknowledge the pause signal and keep supervision. Private card scribing only by agreement; learner keeps it.
Aids for every task
Each task has a short word bank, starter and model. Choose one tier pack; all retain the same outcome and three trials.
Starter
Words: pressure, change, body, thoughts
Start: Stress can affect…
Model: It may affect focus.
Story and meanings
Words: stress, sign, different, clue
Start: In the story, one clue is…
Model: The learner has tense shoulders.
Private hinge
Words: possible, cause, proof, ask
Start: The clue may mean…
Model: It may be stress, but it is not proof.
Story body map
Words: focus, shoulders, stomach
Start: I link… to…
Model: I link tense shoulders to the shoulder area.
Three safe trials
Words: breath, fairer, move, adapt
Start: A safe choice could be…
Model: Use a gentle move within the usual access plan.
Plan and self check
Words: cue, choice, support, alternative
Start: For the story learner…
Model: Ask staff to show the first step.
Review and help
Words: reason, next step, trusted adult
Start: My story answer now shows…
Model: A fairer thought fits what is known.
Prompt ladder

Point to the place or instruction; ask a short private question; rephrase; offer a choice or scaffold; model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time. Record content prompts separately from usual reading, language and communication access.
Checks and planned access
Stress and clues

Stress is a response to pressure or change. It can affect body, thoughts, feelings and actions. Signs vary and can have other causes; the story map cannot diagnose. Reframing checks known facts and tries a fairer view, including real support.
Main hinge and decision

What can the story clues tell us? A: They prove the learner has a condition. B: They may show pressure, but can have other causes. Correct B. If A is chosen, explain that signs alone cannot establish a condition; re-model then use the parallel privately. No public answer round.
Parallel hinge

Which response fits the invented change? A: Check the facts and ask staff to explain the first step. B: Tell the learner to ignore every concern. Correct A. A fairer view can include real support. If unclear, keep the model and revisit later; do not label the learner.
Cognition and Learning
Explicit short definitions, worked example, glossary, visible model, task frames and one chosen step. Flexible grouping for a pair; reduced written load and extra processing time.
Communication and Interaction
Choice, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing, exact scribe and readback. Pair discussion optional; no requirement for speech or eye contact.
SEMH

Predict the sequence, keep all stories invented and mild, offer a quiet supervised pause and supported return. No public feeling check. Story body map and private plan can be blank, fictional or passed; never collect personal details.
Sensory/Physical

Keep the room calm and the usual access and health plans. No induced pressure or noise. Offer one small familiar movement, adapted to access and comfortable range; observing or passing is equal. Breathing stays gentle at own pace, with no holds. Stop discomfort and seek staff help.
EAL

Pre-teach stress, sign and reframing with short plain meanings and the invented story. Allow planning in any language, pointing, glossary and usual language support. No personal explanation is required.
Optional private story checks

F: Point to one possible story clue. M: Explain a fairer thought using the known facts. H: Adapt a strategy if the learner cannot or does not wish to use it. No current-feeling check or public answer round.
Misconceptions
A body clue proves stress. Clues vary and can have other causes; no classroom diagnosis.
A strategy must work for everyone. Access, context and preferences vary. Adapt or ask for support.
Reframing means pretending all is fine. A fairer thought fits facts and can include a real problem and help.
Safe trials and private reflection
Gentle breathing

Sit or stand in your usual supported position. Let an easy breath come in and out at your own pace. Keep breathing comfortable. No hold, forced deep breath, set rate or count. Try briefly, then return to usual breathing. Eyes can stay open. Stop and tell staff if uncomfortable or dizzy. You may observe, use normal breathing or pass.
Reframing

Use the invented thought: “I will get every part wrong.” What is known? The order changed, but the tasks are familiar. Try: “I know some parts. I can ask for the first step.” Say, point to, type or write the fairer thought. A fairer thought need not be cheerful. It must fit the facts. Do not reframe harm as acceptable or dismiss a real problem. Asking for a clearer plan is valid.
Accessible movement

With staff agreement, try one small, familiar move that suits your access plan: a gentle hand move, a seated stretch or a few steps in the agreed clear space. Stay in a comfortable range. No touch, exertion, balance challenge or performance target. Use a familiar alternative or observe/pass. Stop if painful or uncomfortable; follow usual health and access plans.
Private card and self check

Choose one possible strategy for a mild change, privately, or plan for the invented learner. Include practical support. No personal worry, symptom, health or family detail is needed. Keep the card. Blank or pass is valid. One useful choice and a support route. No promise to feel calm and no requirement to cope alone. Strategies do not replace help with the cause of pressure. All boxes start blank. This checks learning, not feelings, symptoms or whether a strategy worked. Observing, adapting or passing is recorded fairly, without a health judgement.
Privacy support and evidence
Discreet supervised pause

Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
Safeguarding and privacy

Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of the lesson pack, book tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school's separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. Private plans are not collected, photographed, displayed or compared for assessment. Scribing the personal plan is only by agreement; the learner keeps it.
Help by type

Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff for help to find an age-appropriate route. Seek help if a concern persists, worsens, affects everyday life or feels unsafe; you do not need a diagnosis first. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school's urgent procedure.
Evidence and marking

Record explanation of stress, three fictional body-map links, a fairer thought, safe strategy knowledge and a generic support route. Record each breathing/reframing/movement opportunity as tried, adapted, observed, passed or not observed; no pass is failure. Do not record symptoms, feelings, private plan content or claimed improvement. Distinguish usual access from actual adult content prompts. Use a work code, one NS and actual pupil response. E requires saved actual work; R requires Voice and Audience plus NS and own response. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.
Where this leads
Next learning applies calm decision-making and help-seeking to safe choices online. Offer fictional learning to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping and evidence sufficiency.

Stress
A response to pressure or change. It can affect the body, thoughts, feelings and actions. A little pressure can help with a task; too much or lasting pressure can make daily life harder.
Sign
A possible clue that someone may feel under pressure. Signs vary and can have other causes. A body map cannot diagnose stress or a condition.
Reframing
Checking a thought against what is known and trying a fairer, more useful way to view the situation. It can include naming a real problem and asking for help.
Invented case key

Meaning
Stress
A response to pressure or change. It may affect body, thoughts, feelings and actions.
Sign
A possible clue. It can have other causes and does not prove a condition.
Reframing
Checking what is known and trying a fairer way to view a situation.
Breathing
Letting air come in and out gently at a comfortable own pace.
Movement
A safe familiar way to move that suits the person and their access plan.
Adapt
Change an option so that it fits the person or situation.
Support
Help from a safe person or route, including help to change a problem.
